SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: KEEPING SAFE
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Keeping Safe helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: KEEPING SAFE
Study Keeping Safe like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping Safe” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Keeping Safe matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Keeping Safe in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Keeping Safe in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Keeping Safe in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Keeping Safe this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Keeping Safe in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Keeping Safe in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Keeping Safe in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Keeping Safe in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping Safe” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Keeping Safe in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Keeping Safe is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping Safe” around your school. (skill: explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Keeping Safe matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Keeping Safe this week. (skill: practise Keeping Safe in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping Safe” around your school. (skill: apply Keeping Safe in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Keeping Safe to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Keeping Safe in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Keeping Safe from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Keeping Safe: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Keeping Safe?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Keeping Safe means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Keeping Safe means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Keeping Safe from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
